newsitem.title: USA: Watson's Royce buy broadens product line.
newsitem.headline: Watson's Royce buy broadens product line.

text.p: Watson Pharmaceuticals' acquisition of Royce Labs, broadens Watson's product line and eliminates a key competitor.
"This is a very good move," said Ronald Stern of Buckingham Research Group. "It gives Watson more product line and (Royce) was a prime competitor of Watson's hydrocodone line of products."
According to Stern, hydrocodone, a narcotic pain-killer, represents about 19 percent of Watson's revenues.

On Thursday, generic drug maker Watson Pharmaceuticals Inc said it was in a definitive agreement to acquire Royce Laboratories Inc also a manufacturer of generic drugs, for $7.25 a share. Watson expected the deal to be accretive to earnings in 1997.
"It's a great deal for both companies," said Adam Greene of Gruntal & Co. "The acquisition should add to earnings. (Watson) has been real wise in mergers in the past," he said.
In September, Watson announced a definitive agreement to acquire Oclassen Pharmaceuticals Inc, a privately held specialty pharmaceutical company, for $135 million.
Watson said it expected that deal to be non-dilutive in 1997.
"Royce has made tremendous strides," Greene continued. "It has grown from a $10 million company to a $20 million company this year."

One trader, referring to the company's previous record of losing money on lower revenues, said: "Royce just became profitable recently and the timing seems good...Royce seems to be getting on more solid ground."
Royce reported profits for the first nine months of 1996 of $0.09 a share on revenues of $17.2 million, compared with loss of $0.12 a share on revenues of $6.5 million the year-ago nine-month period.
Watson traded down 1/4 to 43-1/4 in early afternoon trade.
